facts.text: Falcon grew thanks to the Yazoo and Mississippi Valley Railroad built in the late 19th century, linking Delta farms to markets.
The town sits in the Mississippi Delta, a region whose fertile alluvial soils attracted cotton growers in the mid‑1800s.
After the Great Depression, Falcon saw early adoption of tractors and aerial crop dusting, among the first in Mississippi, reshaping agriculture.
During the civil rights era of the 1950s and 1960s, Quitman County, including Falcon, felt the reverberations of broader struggles for voting rights and desegregation.
Amtrak's City of New Orleans train passes through Falcon on CN tracks but does not stop.
Falcon emerged in a county formed in 1877, carved from neighboring counties to support post‑Civil War agricultural expansion.
